inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ex-CB: 234,371,051 shares in issue at 2026-06-30 less 11,725,600 treasury and 10,064,900 repurchased-pending-cancellation = 212.58m; report-date count implied by the HK$243.7m / HK$1.15 interim dividend = 211.9m; plus 4.27m share-option dilution (H1 FY2026 EPS note) = 216.2m. The US$110m Boyu convertible (conversion HK$37.77, ~22.9m shares) is out of the money at the current price and is carried as DEBT at principal, not as shares -- charging it once. Shares held by the share-award trust (RMB168.8m at cost) are left in the count although SBC is also expensed: a small conservative double-charge. Held flat: SBC expensed in flows; the company is an aggressive repurchaser (RMB432m FY2025, RMB469m H1 FY2026) so the flat count is funded.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual cash-flow statement equity-settled share-based payment add-back (RMB50.5m); no equity-award withholding taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every period). H1 FY2026 SBC RMB33.7m = 2.0% of revenue, the anchor for the forward path.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1724 HKD per CNY, Yahoo CNYHKD=X fetched 2026-10-18 (last trade 2026-10-17). Cross-rate check: USDHKD 7.8479 / USDCNY 6.6768 = 1.1754, a 0.3% tie. Direction check: the Feb-2026 CB proceeds of HK$857.3m booked as RMB761.5m imply 1.126 then, consistent with CNY appreciation since. No dual listing to parity-check against (H-share only). Per-share values computed in CNY and converted to HKD; unsuffixed values are HKD.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Yahoo chart API); 52-week range 24.32-32.28
inputs.wacc_rationale: CNY-built: China 10y CGB ~1.8% + ERP 7.0% x beta 1.0 + 0.5% small-cap/private-healthcare premium = ~9.3% CoE; debt is a small share of capital (bank loans 2.15-3.25%, CB 2% coupon) so WACC ~9.3-9.5%. 9.5% used in all three scenarios -- risk is carried in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash (FY2025 principal RMB123.7m + interest RMB20.5m = RMB144.2m = 4.44% of revenue; H1 FY2026 61.7 + 9.4 = 4.3%) charged through lease_cost_pct_path; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 PP&E + intangibles 66.8m = 2.05%; ROU 121.0m excluded); lease liabilities (RMB500m at 2026-06-30) EXCLUDED from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is small (equity RMB14.7m, H1 FY2026 profit share -RMB1.5m). Flows are consolidated; the NCI book stock is deducted once in equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company -- TCM clinic chain; no bank/REIT/holdco features), with the non-US adaptations (CNY flows / HKD quote, IFRS-16 leases, small NCI). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY entry. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); balance sheet = 30-Jun-2026 interim. NET DEBT RMB142.1m = bank loans 337.8 + convertible bond at principal US$110m x 6.6768 = 734.4 (fair value 695.3 on the balance sheet; principal used because the conversion option is far out of the money and the bond is a redemption claim) + FY2025 final dividend payable 137.1 + declared H1 FY2026 interim dividend HK$243.7m / 1.1724 = 207.9 (stock is ex-dividend at the valuation date; paid ~23-Oct-2026) less cash 1,078.2, time deposits 98.1 and current FVTPL wealth-management products 98.8. Restricted cash (18.4) and the non-current other financial asset (16.4) excluded. The headline '10x debt' is mostly the CB, and the CB proceeds funded RMB469m of buybacks in H1 FY2026 -- cash acquisitions were only RMB65.8m in the half (FY2025 100.0, FY2024 117.5, FY2023 173.2). MID-CYCLE vs LATEST FCF: H1 FY2026 OCF of RMB30.3m is NOT the base: it carries a RMB106m tax payment (including the RMB75m FY2025 tax payable settled in H1) and a working-capital outflow (other payables -109m, receivables +30m, prepayments +64m); H1 is also seasonally the weak half (H1 OCF was 31% and 48% of the full year in FY2024/FY2025). The forward flows are built from components anchored on FY2025 + H1 FY2026 margins, not from either the H1 FCF print or the FY2025 FCF. M&A IS CHARGED: because the growth path includes acquired growth, capex_pct_path includes cash acquisitions (~3.5% of revenue near-term on top of ~3.6% PP&E/intangibles), tapering to 4.0% total as growth slows. H1 FY2026 statutory profit includes a RMB54.6m non-cash CB fair-value gain, excluded from the EBITDA anchor (underlying H1 EBITDA 316.0m pre-SBC-addback). Timing caveat: Y1 = full FY2026 while net debt is at 30-Jun-2026; H1's weak cash flow is already reflected in the lower June net cash, so the overlap is a small conservative double-count.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 8.1% is far below revenue 26.0% and EPS 24.0%: equity is depressed by RMB875m of buybacks and RMB282m of dividends over FY2023-H1 FY2026, not by weak economics. 5yr equity/EPS CAGRs are undefined (negative equity and losses in FY2020 pre-IPO, preferred-share liabilities). Revenue growth has decelerated sharply (+43% FY2023, +30% FY2024, +7.5% FY2025, +10.6% H1 FY2026), so neither the historical revenue nor the equity CAGR is used directly; the base path starts at 11% and fades to 3%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2020 115.6, FY2022 212.1, FY2025 427.8. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are almost identical (SBC fell from 3.1% of revenue in FY2024 to 1.6% in FY2025), so SBC is not eating the growth. Note reported FCF excludes lease cash (~4.4% of revenue) and acquisitions (~3-7% of revenue), both of which the forward build charges.

base.narrative: Densification plus bolt-on M&A and Singapore carry growth near 10% for three years, fading to 3%; adjusted EBITDA margin edges from ~21.8% to 22.5% on scale and membership mix.

bull.narrative: Acquired Beijing/Tianjin/Jinan hospitals integrate cleanly, Singapore becomes a genuine second growth curve, members pass half of revenue; mid-teens growth for two years and margin to 24%.

bear.narrative: M&A spend fails to buy growth: acquired clinics underperform, renowned doctors leave, consumer weakness caps visits; growth falls to low single digits and margin slips to 20% as fixed clinic costs deleverage.

scenario_narratives.base: Gushengtang keeps compounding as China's largest private TCM chain: same-city densification in its 21 core cities, a steady cadence of bolt-on acquisitions (cash M&A of RMB100-175m a year, charged in the flows) and the Singapore build-out deliver ~11% growth in FY2026 (H1 +10.6%) and ~9-10% for two more years before fading to 3% by year 10. The membership programme (>40% of revenue, 85% retention) and the digital prescription/compliance platform lift adjusted EBITDA margin modestly from ~21.8% to 22.5%. Leases (~4.4% of revenue) and M&A spend keep owner-FCF margin in the 5-10% range, well below the reported FCF margin. Leverage is manageable: the US$110m Boyu CB funded buybacks, and group cash still roughly matches borrowings plus the CB and declared dividends.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2026 acquisitions (Beijing Shahe/Hongyang hospitals, Tianjin Bainian Renyitang, Jinan clinics) integrate quickly and lift same-store productivity; Singapore (26 clinics, +1,399% H1) becomes a real second curve via the NTU and 1doc partnerships; policy shifting payment from inpatient to outpatient TCM and an ageing population raise visit frequency. Growth runs 13-14% for two years and stays high single digits to year 6, while operating leverage and member mix take adjusted EBITDA margin to 24%. At HK$37.77 conversion the CB would come into the money -- the bull value is therefore modestly overstated by any conversion dilution above the debt carried.
scenario_narratives.bear: The thesis' two soft spots bite: the doctor-partnership model loses renowned physicians who take their patients, and the acquisition-led growth proves to be bought rather than built -- acquired clinics underperform, goodwill is impaired, and M&A spending continues without lifting revenue growth above low single digits. Fragmented low-price competition and soft discretionary spending in China cap visits; fixed clinic costs deleverage and adjusted EBITDA margin slips to 20%; cash taxes normalise towards the 25% statutory rate as preferential treatment lapses; receivables from insurance reimbursement absorb cash. Debt-funded buybacks leave less balance-sheet room.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: organic growth has visibly slowed (+7.5% FY2025) and the remaining growth is increasingly M&A-funded with key-person (doctor) risk and a CB/debt-funded buyback programme. Base 50% as the central path consistent with H1 FY2026 trading. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- M&A integration, Singapore scaling and margin expansion.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF component DCF in CNY, converted to HKD. Leases are charged as an operating cost and cash acquisitions as capex, because the growth path depends on both; the headline FCF (OCF minus PP&E capex) flatters owners by roughly 7-8% of revenue against that standard. The convertible is treated as debt at principal; buybacks keep the share count flat.
key_risks_to_valuation: M&A treated as recurring capex: if acquisitions stop, growth falls toward the bear path but owner FCF rises -- the two move together
Convertible bond: if the share price rises above HK$37.77, conversion adds ~22.9m shares (~10.6%) instead of the RMB734m debt claim
Cash tax rate: statutory 25% vs ~17% effective; each 2pp is roughly 1% of value
Working capital: the H1 FY2026 outflow is assumed to be timing; a persistent receivables build (insurance settlement) would cut FCF
CNY/HKD rate: per-share HKD value moves 1:1 with the rate
